name: Scandinavian interior
summary: The bright, light-wood room of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. White walls and pale floors catch the short northern daylight; solid-wood furniture with visible joints and wool textiles stand in small groups, and many small lamps replace one ceiling light.

philosophy.core_thesis: A home for a long dark winter must be bright, warm in material and made of few good things that last.
design_principles: Paint walls and ceiling white or pale grey at a light reflectance value of 80 or more, and lay a pale wood floor.
Use one light wood species, oak, ash or birch, for floor and furniture, oiled or soaped to a matt finish.
Light each room with 3–5 small sources at different heights, not one ceiling light: a pendant, a floor lamp, a table lamp and candles.
Keep window sills and the top 30 cm of the window free of curtains, so that the most daylight enters.
Group a sofa and two chairs around a round or oval table on one wool rug.
Add warmth with texture, not colour: wool, sheepskin, linen and a knitted throw on the seats.
Limit accents to 5% of the surface, in muted blue, sage, ochre or black.
anti_patterns: Dark walls or dark floors that absorb the daylight
Heavy drapes that cover the window head
One bright ceiling light as the only source
Gloss lacquer, chrome and mirrored surfaces
Saturated colour on more than one large surface

composition.plan_logic: Small furniture groups around low tables. The room stays open toward the windows, and the wall opposite the window holds the storage.
composition.focal_point: The window and its daylight, or a wood stove; the eye goes to the brightest plane of the room.

rules.rule: Make the window the focal point. Put the main seats so that they face it or stand at 90 degrees to it.
Balance a sofa on one side with two light chairs and a floor lamp on the other.
Show the repeat of the floorboards and of the wood battens or chair spindles.
Keep the contrast between walls and floor low; one black line, such as a lamp or a frame, gives the edge.
rules.value: wall to floor LRV difference 30 or less

rules.rule: Group lamps, candles and plants in clusters of 3 at different heights.
Layer textiles on the seats: a throw, a cushion and a sheepskin in different weaves of one colour family.
Leave the walls mostly bare and the floor open between the groups.
Mark each zone with a rug and a pendant: sit, eat, read.
Keep the route from the door to the window clear.
Keep the window wall free of tall furniture, so that the view from the door ends in daylight.
rules.value: 0 tall pieces on the window wall

rules.rule: Give white and pale grey the walls, pale wood and grey wool the secondary share, and one muted colour the accents.
Use 3–5 low sources per room at warm white, with glare-free shades.
Use one wood species for floor and furniture; vary the textiles only.
Shoot the room level, with a two-point view toward the window at 20–30 degrees.

zoning.circulation: One route from the door to the window and a loop around the dining table.

palette.distribution: White walls and ceiling; pale oak floor and furniture; grey and off-white wool textiles; one muted accent on a cushion, a vase or a print; black in thin lines.

lighting.strategy: Many small warm sources at different heights make pools of light. Shades hide the lamp and stop glare.
lighting.daylight: Large windows with bare heads and white reveals; sheer linen at most. Window glass is 20% of the floor area.

layers.source: floor lamp with a fabric shade

materials.finish: White oil or soap on wood, matt paint on walls. Nothing is glossy.
materials.texture_contrast: Smooth pale wood against soft wool and knit, at about 2:1 by area.

furniture.silhouette: Light frames of solid wood with rounded edges and visible joints; spindle and paper-cord seats; legs on show.
furniture.arrangement: A sofa with two chairs around a round or oval low table on a wool rug; a dining table with mixed chairs under a pendant.

textiles.pattern: Plain weaves and soft texture; one simple stripe or check on a rug or a throw at most.
textiles.windows: Bare windows or light linen sheers that leave the window head free.

objects.approach: Few, useful and hand-made objects: ceramics, candle holders, a plant, a stack of books.
objects.grouping: Groups of 3 at different heights on a sill or a sideboard; one leaning print on a picture ledge.

implementation.brief: A white living room with a pale oak floor and a large window. A grey wool sofa and two paper-cord chairs stand around a round oak table on a pale rug; a glare-free pendant, a floor lamp and candles light the room.
implementation.image_prompt: Scandinavian living room, white walls, pale oak floorboards, large window with bare head and sheer linen, light grey wool sofa, two wishbone chairs with paper-cord seats, round oak coffee table, pale wool rug, sheepskin, glare-free pendant lamp, candles on the sill, plants, soft northern daylight, calm, editorial photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Dark walls, heavy drapes, gloss, chrome, saturated colour, clutter, ornate furniture, single harsh ceiling light.
implementation.camera: 28 mm lens, camera at 130 cm, two-point view toward the window at 20–30 degrees.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 550 x 420 cm, ceiling 260 cm. Overcast sky through one 200 x 180 cm window; 4 point lights at 2700 K at 45, 75, 140 and 180 cm.

emotion.target_response: Bright calm: the viewer feels a light, tidy home that is warm to touch and easy to live in.

avoid_when: The brief asks for drama, luxury or strong colour.
The room has hot direct sun all day and needs shade more than reflected light.

modifiers.how: Lower the furniture to 38 cm seats, add one dark wood and stoneware, reduce objects to 1–3 per surface; keep the pale walls and the natural textiles.
Change oak to teak, add a mustard or teal accent and an arc lamp; keep the legs on show.
Paint one wall and its trim in a saturated hue and raise accents to 25%; keep the wood floor.

sources.title: Charlotte and Peter Fiell, Scandinavian Design (Taschen, 2002)
Design in Scandinavia: An Exhibition of Objects for the Home (travelling exhibition catalogue, United States and Canada, 1954–1957)
